meaning: Seen or found everywhere
trick: UBIQUITOUS: 'You BE QUICK, it's everywhere!'
examples: Massoud's handsome face would become ubiquitous in Kabul.
Mobile phones are ubiquitous these days.

meaning: The bag-like parts under cows, goats and similar animals that hold milk
trick: UDDERS: the cow's UDDERS give milk to OTHERS.
examples: They had not been milked for a day, and their udders were almost bursting.
The farmer cleaned the cow's udders before milking.

meaning: (Of a reason) kept hidden, not the one you say
trick: ULTERIOR motive = a motive kept INTERIOR (inside, hidden).
examples: Communication with no strings attached and no ulterior motive.
I think he is being kind with an ulterior motive.

meaning: A final demand that comes with a threat if it is not met
trick: ULTIMATUM = the ULTIMATE (last) warning.
examples: My wife had given me an ultimatum, and now I had a decision to make.
The boss gave him an ultimatum: improve or leave.

usage.pattern: give someone an ultimatum / issue an ultimatum

meaning: Informal: ultramarathons, races longer than a marathon
trick: ULTRAS = ULTRA-long runs.
examples: I wasn't even thinking about ultras yet.
She started running ultras after her first marathon.

meaning: Not used to something
trick: UN + ACCUSTOMED: NOT ACCUSTOMED (not a CUSTOM for you).
examples: She was unaccustomed to the Kabuli dialect of his Farsi.
I am unaccustomed to waking up so early.

usage.pattern: be unaccustomed to something / to doing something

meaning: Agreed by everyone
trick: UNANIMOUS: UN (one) + ANIMUS (mind): ONE MIND, sabki sahmati.
examples: A unanimous resolution was passed that the farmhouse should be a museum.
The vote was unanimous.

meaning: Too strong to be questioned or defeated
trick: UN-ASSAIL-ABLE: no one is ABLE to ASSAIL (attack) it.
examples: She sobbed like a child overwhelmed by an adult's unassailable logic.
The team built an unassailable lead.

meaning: Coming without being asked for or wanted
trick: UN-BIDDEN: not BIDDEN (not invited).
examples: But then some memory would rise, unbidden.
Tears came unbidden to her eyes.

meaning: In a strange way that is hard to explain
hindi: अजीब तरह से, विचित्र रूप से
trick: UNCANNILY: you CAN'T explain how.
examples: Simple, and yet uncannily effective.
She looks uncannily like her grandmother.

meaning: In a rude, sudden way, without politeness
trick: UN-CEREMONY: no ceremony, no politeness at all.
examples: The manager unceremoniously told him to leave and find another band.
He was unceremoniously pushed out of the room.

meaning: Clear and not confused; also clear, without clouds
trick: UN-CLOUDED: no CLOUDS in the mind.
examples: Laila was grateful that Mariam was in charge, unclouded and sober.
After a good sleep, my mind felt unclouded.

usage.pattern: unclouded by something / an unclouded mind

meaning: Not put off or afraid despite difficulty
trick: UN-DAUNTED: not DAUNTED (not scared off).
examples: Undaunted by the chilly weather, families flooded the city.
Undaunted by failure, she tried again.

meaning: A jaw where the lower teeth stick out in front of the upper teeth
trick: UNDER-BITE: the UNDER teeth BITE in front.
examples: He was thick, tall, and had a severe underbite.
The dentist said my son has a slight underbite.

meaning: Not given enough food
trick: UNDER-FED: FED UNDER the needed amount.
examples: The fields were full of weeds and the animals were underfed.
The stray dog looked thin and underfed.

meaning: Having too little salt
trick: UNDER-SALTED: SALT is UNDER the right level.
examples: A little undersalted but good.
The soup was slightly undersalted.

meaning: To take on a task or responsibility and start doing it
trick: UNDER-TAKE: TAKE a job UNDER your care.
examples: It is perhaps the most worthy struggle one can undertake in life.
The company will undertake a new project next month.

usage.pattern: undertake something / undertake to do something

meaning: A person whose job is to prepare dead bodies and arrange funerals
hindi: कफ़न-दफ़न करने वाला, अंतिम संस्कार कराने वाला
trick: UNDERTAKER: he TAKES the dead body UNDER the ground.
examples: The undertaker's man turned to me and said something I didn't catch.
The family called the undertaker to arrange the funeral.

usage.pattern: call the undertaker / the undertaker's men

meaning: Not yet decided or found out
trick: UN-DETERMINED: not yet DETERMINED.
examples: My true potential was still undetermined.
The cause of the fire is still undetermined.

meaning: A feeling of worry or discomfort
trick: UN-EASE: NOT at EASE.
examples: Dissatisfaction and unease are part of human nature.
I felt a sense of unease when he didn't call.

usage.pattern: a sense/feeling of unease / unease about something

meaning: Always right or accurate
trick: UN-ERRING: never ERRS (never makes an error).
examples: That obsession stems from an unerring belief that they are not that great.
She has an unerring sense of direction.

meaning: Too strange or deep to understand
trick: UN-FATHOM-ABLE: you can't FATHOM (measure the depth of) it.
examples: She couldn't get around the unfathomable reality that Giti was gone.
Why he quit his job is unfathomable to me.

usage.pattern: unfathomable + noun / be unfathomable to someone

meaning: Not worried or upset by something
trick: UN-FAZED: nothing FAZES him, cool as ice.
examples: After the war they felt more grateful and unfazed by petty annoyances.
She was unfazed by the large crowd.

meaning: Without showing fear or hesitation, even when it is hard
trick: UN-FLINCH-INGLY: without FLINCHING (pulling back).
examples: He was able to be completely, unflinchingly honest with himself.
She looked unflinchingly at the angry crowd.

usage.pattern: unflinchingly + honest / look unflinchingly at something

meaning: To open out or spread out from a rolled or folded state
trick: UN-FURL: a FURLED (rolled) flag UNrolls.
examples: I could see it unfurl from the top of the pass.
The sailors began to unfurl the sails.

meaning: Without anything getting in the way
trick: UN-HINDERED: nothing HINDERS (blocks) you.
examples: The days of unhindered playing in the streets with Tariq had passed.
The ambulance drove through the city unhindered.

meaning: Mentally unbalanced or wildly upset
trick: UN-HINGED: a door off its HINGES, swinging wildly.
examples: Laila was shocked at how easily she'd come unhinged.
He started shouting like an unhinged man.

meaning: Imaginary white horses with one horn; 'roses and ...' = perfect and happy
trick: UNI-CORNS: UNI (one) + CORN (horn).
examples: It can't all be roses and unicorns all the time.
My daughter loves stories about unicorns.

usage.pattern: roses and unicorns / rainbows and unicorns

meaning: Acting freely without shyness or holding back
trick: UN-INHIBITED: no INHIBITIONS, totally free.
examples: Mariam watched them walking uninhibited down the street.
The children danced in an uninhibited way.

meaning: Doing or saying something at the same time, together
trick: UNI-SON = one sound: everyone sounds as ONE.
examples: The whole farm burst out into Beasts of England in tremendous unison.
The children said 'Good morning' in unison.

usage.pattern: in unison / in unison with someone

meaning: Not fair or morally right
trick: UN + JUST = not just = not fair.
examples: Despite the unjust cruelties of our world, the heroines do endure.
It is unjust to punish the whole class for one boy's mistake.

usage.pattern: unjust + noun / it is unjust to do something

meaning: Untidy and not looked after
trick: UN-KEMPT = not 'kempt' (combed) - nobody combed or kept it neat.
examples: Mariam found herself in a small, unkempt yard where yellow grass grew in thin patches.
He came to work with unkempt hair and a crumpled shirt.

meaning: Suddenly let out a strong force or feeling
trick: UN-LEASH-ED = took the dog off its LEASH - it rushed out.
examples: The words packed a fierce potency, and she unleashed them now.
The storm unleashed heavy rain on the city.

meaning: Making someone feel nervous, uneasy or less confident
trick: UN-NERV-ING = takes away your NERVE.
examples: The loss of side vision was unnerving, and she did not like the cloth pressing against her mouth.
It was unnerving to hear footsteps in the empty house.

meaning: Not covered with a hard surface like tar or stone
trick: UN-PAVED = no PAVEMENT, just dirt.
examples: Mariam quickly looked over the narrow, unpaved road where Rasheed's house stood.
The bus bumped along the unpaved village road.

meaning: Informal: to untwist or straighten something, especially your confused thinking
trick: A PRETZEL is a twisted snack - UN-PRETZEL = untwist it.
examples: I'll give you a minute to unpretzel your brain and read that again.
Take a deep breath and unpretzel your thoughts before you answer.

meaning: Coming apart thread by thread; also slowly falling apart or failing; US spelling
trick: UN-RAVEL-ING: a knitted sweater UNRAVELS when you pull one thread.
examples: Laila pictured her life as a rotted rope, snapping, unraveling, the fibers falling away.
The old rope was unraveling at one end.

meaning: Makes something come apart thread by thread; also solves or explains something confusing
hindi: उधेड़ देता है, बिखेर देता है; सुलझाता है
trick: UN-RAVEL-S: pull one thread and the whole sweater UNRAVELS.
examples: Trying to tear pain out of life unravels everything else with it.
The detective slowly unravels the mystery.

meaning: Not becoming weaker or less strong; continuing without a break
trick: UN-RELENT-ING = never RELENTS (never gives up or softens).
examples: Then there were days when the dreariness didn't seem quite as unrelenting to Mariam.
The unrelenting heat made everyone tired.

meaning: Continuing without stopping or getting less
trick: UN-REMIT-TING = never REMITS (never pauses or lets off).
examples: The ache of his absence was her unremitting companion.
The nurses worked with unremitting care through the night.

meaning: Difficult to control or manage; behaving badly
trick: UN-RULY = won't follow the RULES.
examples: Is it your teacher or coach, your boss, an unruly client?
The teacher calmed the unruly class.

meaning: Not hurt or damaged at all
trick: UN-SCATHED: no SCAR, no SCRATCH.
examples: But the men did not go unscathed either.
Luckily, the driver walked away from the crash unscathed.

meaning: In a way that shows someone is looking but not noticing, often lost in thought
trick: UN-SEE-ING-LY: eyes open, but not SEEING.
examples: Jalil slouched in his chair, looking unseeingly at the pitcher on the table.
She stared unseeingly out of the window, thinking of home.

meaning: To free someone or something from chains or limits
trick: UN + SHACKLE: take off the SHACKLES (chains).
examples: Mission: to unshackle your mind.
Good teachers unshackle students from fear of mistakes.

meaning: Not having a nice or neat shape
trick: UN-SHAPELY = no nice SHAPE.
examples: Mariam saw her own face first, the archless, unshapely eyebrows, the flat hair.
The tailor fixed the unshapely old coat.

meaning: Given or sent without being asked for
trick: UN-SOLICIT-ED = nobody SOLICITED (asked for) it.
examples: If you try to break out of their box, you'll get some unsolicited advice.
I keep getting unsolicited emails from shops.

meaning: Not yet walked on or visited by people
trick: UN-TROD-DEN: no feet have TROD (walked) here.
examples: The fields of England should be untrodden by human feet.
We found an untrodden path through the snowy forest.

meaning: Not covered with a veil; also shown to the public for the first time
trick: UN-VEIL-ED: the VEIL is off.
examples: Talibs patrolled the city on the lookout for the loud laugh, the unveiled face.
The company unveiled its new phone today.

usage.pattern: an unveiled face / unveil something (to someone)

meaning: Not changing or becoming weaker; firm and steady
trick: UN-WAVER-ING = never WAVERS (never shakes).
examples: They must feel an unwavering certainty in their own righteousness.
Thanks for your unwavering support.

meaning: Not knowing what is really happening or what you are doing
trick: UN-WIT-TING = no WIT of it (no idea).
examples: Now here was his unwitting accomplice, thinking our first negotiator was still in charge.
She became an unwitting part of the prank.

meaning: Very hard and not bending; also not changing your mind
trick: UN-YIELD-ING = does not YIELD (give way).
examples: The ground had hardened like a rock, the dirt unyielding.
She stayed unyielding in her demand for justice.

meaning: Someone's duty or decision to do something
trick: UP TO YOU = the ball is in YOUR court.
examples: It was up to him to express his sympathy and so forth.
Where we eat tonight is up to you.

usage.pattern: it is up to someone (to do something)

meaning: Turned over so the top is at the bottom
trick: UP-ENDED: the END that was down is now UP.
examples: The charred husks of cars lay upended, sometimes stacked on top of each other.
The dog upended the bin and spread rubbish everywhere.

meaning: (Of furniture) covered with soft padding and cloth or leather
trick: UP-HOLSTER-ED: chairs wearing a soft HOLSTER (cover).
examples: Two couches were upholstered in beige suede.
We bought an upholstered chair for the reading corner.

meaning: Sitting or standing straight; also honest and good
trick: UP-RIGHT: standing UP, perfectly RIGHT (straight).
examples: Fifteen minutes later I was upright, in the saddle, and climbing into the lava fields.
Please sit upright during the meeting.

meaning: Loud noise and confusion; also strong public anger
trick: UP-ROAR: everyone ROARS UP at once.
examples: Unfortunately, the uproar woke up Mr. Jones.
The new rule caused an uproar among parents.

usage.pattern: cause an uproar / an uproar over something

meaning: In a very loud and noisy way, especially with laughter
trick: UPROAR-IOUSLY: laughing so loud it's an UPROAR.
examples: Then he laughed again, uproariously this time.
The audience laughed uproariously at the joke.

meaning: To leave your home and move somewhere new; also to pull a plant out with its roots
hindi: घर छोड़ना, उखड़ना; जड़ से उखाड़ना
trick: UP + ROOT: pull your ROOTS UP and go.
examples: She invited me to uproot across the country and move in with her.
The storm uprooted many old trees.

meaning: New and trying to become important, often seen as too bold
trick: UP-START: just STARTED and already acting UP.
examples: Record contracts didn't fall from the sky, especially for raucous, upstart metal bands.
The upstart company beat the big brands.

meaning: Polite, confident and refined in manner, like a city person
trick: URBANE = URBAN manners: smooth city style.
examples: How urbane, how Tajik, of you.
The urbane host made every guest feel at ease.

meaning: To lead or guide someone somewhere
trick: USHER at a cinema shows you to your seat.
examples: It took Laila some work to get the children to form a queue and to usher them into the classroom.
The guard ushered us into the hall.

meaning: Tools or containers used in the kitchen, such as pots and spoons
trick: UTENSILS - Use Them Every day in the kitchen (U-T-E).
examples: The cupboards were full of unfamiliar utensils.
Please wash the utensils after dinner.
